assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy opened a new class of medicines that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. The chain from peptide biology to approved drugs is clear, original and of very large patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic proof of concept) and Mojsov (identification of the active truncated GLP-1 form) are the strongest scientific trio. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is an industrial-translation contributor, so the choice of three involves a real trade-off, and the priority question around Mojsov is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of clinical use, large outcome trials and independent replication; recognition is timely given the current clinical scale.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among basic discoverers and drug developers is unresolved.
Some long-term safety and durability questions are still being studied; I have not independently verified recent trial details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV provide primary prevention of cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population-level reductions in infection and precancer. A clear, original discovery with major, demonstrated public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller established L1 VLP self-assembly and its immunogenicity; Frazer (with Zhou) contributed early VLP expression and vaccine development. Other contributors (e.g. Zhou, deceased) and the zur Hausen cervical-cancer link already honoured in 2008 complicate allocation but a trio is supportable.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: licensed since 2006, with strong real-world effectiveness data from several countries.
uncertainties: Credit between the NCI and Queensland groups has had priority disputes; I cannot verify details independently.
Deceased contributors cannot share a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as the dominant driver of cytokine cascades in rheumatoid synovium and demonstration in patients that TNF blockade works established anti-cytokine therapy and changed outcomes across rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. A paradigm shift from concept to clinic.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the mechanistic work and the first clinical trials; the pair is a clean, well-defined configuration. Related contributions on TNF cloning and antibody engineering by others exist but the translational concept is theirs.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of use, extensive independent confirmation and biosimilar-era scale.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as mainly translational medicine versus a basic discovery.
Contributions of other TNF and antibody-engineering researchers could be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a causal tool for controlling genetically specified cells with light and has reshaped circuit-level physiology worldwide, with early clinical applications emerging (e.g. vision restoration).
assessment.attribution: Discovery and characterisation of channelrhodopsins (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and their adaptation to neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth; also Miesenböck's earlier approach) form a six-person field; prize rules require trimming. Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel cover the molecular discovery and the key mammalian-neuron/behavior demonstrations, but this omits Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research technology, with widespread independent adoption; therapeutic impact is still early.
uncertainties: Attribution is the main obstacle: at most three of six or more deserving people.
Clinical impact is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as the founding regulator of apoptosis linked cell-death control to cancer and underpins venetoclax, a targeted drug for CLL and other leukaemias. Fundamental discovery with clear clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams characterised the BCL-2 family and its pro-survival function; Vaux showed BCL-2 as a cell-death inhibitor and cooperating oncogene. Strasser is a major later contributor. Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Green/Reed contributed to the early BCL-2 story and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: robust confirmation, mechanism defined, approved drugs in use. Apoptosis was recognised in 2002, so novelty relative to that prize is a consideration.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize (cell death genetics) may reduce perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality for cancer, with growing use in autoimmune disease as well.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CAR design), June (4-1BB CAR and clinical translation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early clinical CAR/TCR trials) are a plausible trio; Eshhar's earlier CAR concept is not credited in this list.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: approved products and years of follow-up, but toxicity, access and solid-tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Possible omission of Zelig Eshhar from the proposed configuration.
Long-term durability and safety are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the T- and B-lymphocyte lineages and their distinct roles in adaptive immunity is a foundational discovery on which much of modern immunology and immunotherapy rests.
assessment.attribution: Miller established the thymus as the source of T-cell function; Cooper defined the bursal/B-cell and the two-lineage concept with Good. Good (deceased) shared earlier credit. The two-person configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and unquestioned; the question is timing and age of the laureates rather than evidence.
uncertainties: Advanced age of the laureates and prior recognition via Lasker/other prizes.
The Nobel Committee's weighting of historical versus contemporary work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and interferon responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity (e.g. interferonopathies, lupus), and cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger (with Sun); Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa and Wu are further credited names. Proposed trio is a reasonable but contestable subset.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: mechanism strongly confirmed; clinical translation (STING agonists/antagonists) has not yet succeeded.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between STING discovery groups and cGAS discovery.
